summary: The 1987 tower at the end of Pentwater's north pier, Michigan, marking the channel's north side with a flashing green light and a fog signal.

structures.note: Placed on the north pier by a National Guard Chinook helicopter on 8 October 1987; prefabricated, 12,000 lb, made in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Height reported as 25 ft (Herald-Journal) or 30 ft (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Walk the beach from Charles Mears State Park to the north pier.

corrections.why: The north tower was placed on 8 October 1987 (LighthouseFriends, citing the Ludington Daily News of 9 October 1987; the Herald-Journal also gives 1987). The 1997 date comes from Terry Pepper's history and from the Wikidata entry, and does not match the newspaper.

corrections.proposed: not settled: 7.6 m (25 ft, Herald-Journal) or 9.1 m (30 ft, LighthouseFriends)
corrections.why: Two sources give different heights and neither gives 11 m (36 ft).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Terry Pepper's history and the Wikidata record give 1997 for the north tower. LighthouseFriends, citing the Ludington Daily News of 9 October 1987 and the placement on 8 October 1987, and the Herald-Journal column both give 1987. This research follows 1987. Terry Pepper's 1997 is probably an error carried into later sources, but no source read says so directly.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: none assigned to this station. The USLHS roster that the lookup printed for 'Pentwater Pierhead' (Francis McGuire, Annie McGuire, Barney Evers, Andrew J. Davenport, William P. Larson, John Davenport, 1873-1915) belongs to the 1873 light on the SOUTH pier, the record us-mi-pentwater (Pentwater Light / South Pierhead; the south-pierhead record is hidden as a duplicate). The lookup matched this station by name and position at 0.77 km, but the USLHS place sits at 43.7762, -86.4400, which is the south pier. Do not attach that roster to this station. Keeper dates also differ between sources for the south light (Terry Pepper: Annie McGuire removed 1887 and Barney Evers appointed 1887; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS roster: 1885); that matters for us-mi-pentwater, not here. Date conflict: 1997 (Terry Pepper, Wikidata, Wikipedia's lead) vs 1987 (LighthouseFriends with the Ludington Daily News of 9 October 1987 'Pentwater finally has a lighthouse' by Todd Reed, which was not read directly; the Herald-Journal column; the station record's Rowlett date). The story follows 1987; the newspaper should be checked if anyone can reach the Ludington Daily News archive. Height conflict: 25 ft (Herald-Journal), 30 ft (LighthouseFriends), 36 ft (record, from Wikidata). Characteristic: the record gives Fl G 2.5s from ENC; Terry Pepper says flashing green; no source read gives the 2.5 s period, so the story uses 'flashing green'. Material: the record says concrete; no source read gives the north tower's material (the Wikipedia lead's infobox is not used), so none is given. NRHP: the harbor navigation structures are said to be listed in 2001 (Wikipedia lead; Wikidata), but the NPS nomination and the NPS record were not readable (placeholder and empty page), so the listing is left out of the story. Life-Saving Service: the 1880 report (scan p. 53) lists 'one at or near Pentwater, Lake Michigan' among the stations a bill provides for, and says those stations were recommended in the last annual report; no source read shows it established, so the story says 'among stations a bill would establish'; the Wikipedia lead says a station was built on the north pier in 1887 (not cited; not confirmed); no station record for the Pentwater life-saving station exists in data/stations, so it may need one. Photo: the record's photo file (Pentwater_Walkin_the_Beach) does not show the light; check before use. The Herald-Journal column is undated and its author is not named in the text read. Appropriation year: the Herald-Journal says Congress appropriated $55,000 in 1857, in the year the channel was dug (c. 1857); Terry Pepper (6 March 1867) and LighthouseFriends give 1867. The story states both dates and does not choose; no source read explains the difference. Website: the Herald-Journal names visitpentwater.com, not the village, so the story does not call it the village's site.
